text: This book unveils Jesus Christ, whom God sent through an angel to John.
John reports what he saw as God's word.
A blessing rests on those who read it aloud and heed it.
John writes to seven churches in Asia, with greetings from the eternal God.
Greetings also come from Jesus, the faithful witness and ruler of kings, who freed us.
He made us a kingdom and priests to his God.
He is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him.
God declares he is the beginning and the end.
John shares in their suffering and was on Patmos for the word of God.
On the Lord's Day John heard a trumpet-like voice behind him.
It told him to write what he sees and send it to seven named cities.
He turned and saw seven golden lampstands.
Among them stood one like a son of man in a long robe.
His hair was white as wool and his eyes like fire.
His feet gleamed like bronze and his voice roared like water.
He held seven stars, and a sharp sword came from his mouth.
John fell as if dead, but the figure touched him and told him not to fear.
He is the living one who died and now holds the keys of death.
John must write what he has seen, what is, and what will come.
The stars are the churches' angels, and the lampstands are the churches.
